definitions.gloss: prepared side dish; ready-made dish; deli food
definitions.explanation: Cooked dishes sold ready to eat, typically found at supermarkets, department store basements (depachika), and specialty shops. Includes items like fried chicken, salads, simmered vegetables, and more.

examples.japanese: {今日|きょう}は{総菜|そうざい}を{買|か}って{帰|かえ}ろう。
examples.english: Let's buy some deli food on the way home today.

examples.japanese: スーパーの{総菜|そうざい}コーナーは{夕方|ゆうがた}になると{安|やす}くなる。
examples.english: The deli section at the supermarket gets cheaper in the evening.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しい{日|ひ}は{総菜|そうざい}に{頼|たよ}ることが{多|おお}いが、{栄養|えいよう}バランスには{気|き}をつけている。
examples.english: On busy days I often rely on prepared dishes, but I try to watch the nutritional balance.

notes:
USAGE:
A very common word in daily Japanese life. Also written as お{惣菜|そうざい} with the polite prefix お. Supermarkets and department store basements ({地下|ちか}, commonly called デパ{地下|ちか}) have extensive {総菜|そうざい} sections.

ORTHOGRAPHY:
Also written as {惣菜|そうざい}. Both kanji forms are common.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {総菜|そうざい}を{買|か}う (to buy prepared food)
- {総菜|そうざい}コーナー (deli section)
- {手作|てづく}り{総菜|そうざい} (homemade side dishes)
